capabilities.name: Credit Terms / Payment on Account
capabilities.description: Business customers can receive goods before paying, on agreed credit terms (e.g. net 30/60/90) up to a credit limit.

capabilities.name: Company Buyer Roles
capabilities.description: A business customer's own company has multiple people with different purchasing roles (e.g. requester vs. approver) under one company account.

capabilities.name: Subscription Commerce
capabilities.description: The system sells recurring subscription products or services to end customers (distinct from the platform's own operator billing).

capabilities.name: Subscription Pause/Skip
capabilities.description: Customers can pause or skip an upcoming subscription cycle without fully cancelling.

capabilities.name: Subscription Upgrade/Downgrade
capabilities.description: Customers can change their subscription plan (upgrade or downgrade) with the price difference prorated.

capabilities.name: Failed Payment Recovery (Dunning)
capabilities.description: When a recurring payment fails, the system automatically retries and notifies the customer before cancelling the subscription.

capabilities.name: Loyalty Points / Rewards
capabilities.description: Customers earn points or rewards for purchases or other qualifying actions.

capabilities.name: Loyalty Membership Tiers
capabilities.description: Customers are grouped into membership tiers (e.g. silver/gold/VIP) with different benefits.

capabilities.name: Referral Rewards
capabilities.description: Customers are rewarded for referring new customers who go on to complete a qualifying purchase.

capabilities.name: Gift Cards / Store Credit
capabilities.description: Customers can hold and redeem store credit or gift card balances. Requires CAP-COMMERCIAL, not CAP-PAYMENTS specifically: a gift card balance is redeemed against a transaction total regardless of whether the underlying purchase (of the card itself, or of what it's redeemed for) is paid online or offline.

capabilities.name: Product / Store Reviews
capabilities.description: Customers can leave ratings and written reviews for products or the store.

capabilities.name: Photo/Video Reviews
capabilities.description: Customers can attach photos or videos to their reviews.

capabilities.name: Review Moderation
capabilities.description: Reviews must be approved before they are published publicly.

capabilities.name: Review Request Campaigns
capabilities.description: The system proactively invites customers to leave a review after their purchase, rather than waiting for unprompted reviews.

capabilities.name: Cross-Border Trade
capabilities.description: Products are sold across national borders and involve import/export customs processes, distinct from domestic-only sales.

capabilities.name: HS Code / Tariff Classification
capabilities.description: Products carry a customs tariff classification code (HS code) as part of their master data, since it directly affects the duty rate. This only assigns a classification code to the product; it never computes or sets what the customer pays -- that calculation is CAP-LANDED-COST's scope, which is why this capability carries no Q-COM-001 ('charges customers') gate: HS classification applies to any cross-border product movement, commercial or not.

capabilities.name: Duties / Landed Cost Calculation
capabilities.description: The system calculates import duties/taxes so the customer sees the total landed cost, not just the product price. Requires CAP-TAX (which itself requires CAP-COMMERCIAL), not CAP-PAYMENTS directly: showing the landed-cost total is a calculation/display concern independent of whether the order is ultimately paid online or through an offline channel.

capabilities.name: Product Compliance Registry (e.g. Digital Product Passport)
capabilities.description: Products must be registered in a destination market's product compliance/passport registry before they can be sold there.

capabilities.name: Order Split / Partial Fulfillment
capabilities.description: A single order can be fulfilled as multiple separate shipments (e.g. from different warehouses, or partial-now/rest-later).

capabilities.name: Backorder Support
capabilities.description: Customers can order out-of-stock items, which ship once restocked, rather than being blocked from ordering.

capabilities.name: Preorder Support
capabilities.description: Customers can order products before they are officially released or in stock.

capabilities.name: Dropship Fulfillment
capabilities.description: Some orders are shipped directly by the supplier to the customer rather than through the merchant's own warehouse.

capabilities.name: Demand Forecasting
capabilities.description: The system predicts future sales volume to support inventory planning, rather than planning being based purely on gut feel.

capabilities.name: Automated Reorder Recommendations
capabilities.description: The system automatically recommends when and how much to reorder based on forecasted demand, lead time, and safety stock.

capabilities.name: Influencer / Creator Partnerships
capabilities.description: The business works with influencers or content creators who promote products in exchange for compensation.

capabilities.name: Affiliate Program
capabilities.description: External affiliate partners earn a commission for sales they refer.

capabilities.name: Affiliate/Influencer Attribution Tracking
capabilities.description: Each referral link or promo code's actual resulting sales and commission are tracked, not just estimated.

capabilities.name: Physical Retail POS
capabilities.description: The business sells through physical retail locations, pop-ups, or events using a point-of-sale system.

capabilities.name: POS/Online Inventory Sync
capabilities.description: In-store inventory is kept in sync with online inventory from one canonical stock record.

capabilities.name: Click & Collect / Ship-from-Store
capabilities.description: Customers can order online and pick up in-store, or have a store location ship the order to them.

capabilities.name: Returns / RMA Workflow
capabilities.description: Customers can request a post-purchase return or exchange (not tied to a product defect) that goes through request, approval, return shipment, receiving inspection, and a refund-or-exchange handoff, distinct from both warranty claims and raw refund execution.

capabilities.name: Product Warranty Tracking
capabilities.description: Products carry a warranty period and customers can file a warranty claim within it.

capabilities.name: Repair / Replacement Case Tracking
capabilities.description: Repair or replacement cases are tracked through a defined status workflow from intake to resolution.

capabilities.name: Cross-Channel Identity Resolution
capabilities.description: The same real customer contacting the business through different channels (email, chat apps, different platform accounts) is automatically recognized as one person, with conservative auto-merge and a manual review path for uncertain matches.

capabilities.name: Marketing Consent Ledger
capabilities.description: The customer's consent status for each marketing channel and purpose is recorded as an auditable history, not just a single current-state flag, to support opt-out and compliance audits.

capabilities.name: Promotions / Coupons
capabilities.description: A discount -- a time-limited sale, a coupon code, or a spend-threshold markdown -- is scoped to specific catalog items and applied against a transaction's total at checkout, reducing the amount owed without altering the item's own base price.

capabilities.name: Conditional Promotion Rules
capabilities.description: A promotion can carry conditional logic beyond a flat markdown -- buy-X-get-Y, multi-item bundle pricing, or a spend-threshold trigger -- rather than a single unconditional discount amount.

capabilities.name: Channel / Market Price Books
capabilities.description: The same product is priced differently depending on the sales channel (e.g. own site vs. a marketplace) or market it sells in, driven by a price book rather than one single price applied everywhere.

capabilities.name: Order / Transaction Abuse Screening
capabilities.description: Suspicious orders are flagged for manual review using rules -- velocity limits, blacklist/allowlist membership, and promo, referral, or return abuse patterns -- keyed to a customer identity rather than an order in isolation. Raw card-level payment fraud scoring is explicitly out of scope and is delegated to the payment provider (e.g. Stripe Radar); account takeover / credential-compromise detection is also explicitly out of scope here and is a session/credential security concern (see DER-SESSION), not an order-abuse rule; this capability only covers first-party transaction-abuse signals a PSP cannot see. Distinct from CAP-FINANCIAL-DECISION, which per Q-REG-002 is scoped to lending/credit/insurance-eligibility decisions about a person, not order-abuse flags.

capabilities.name: Chargeback / Dispute Case Management
capabilities.description: A card-network chargeback or payment dispute is tracked as a case referencing the original order, payment, and customer, from case creation through evidence submission to a won/lost outcome. A lost or refund-owed outcome is settled through CAP-REFUNDS' normal refund workflow, never a silent balance adjustment outside it. Scoped to disputes on the online/card-not-present payments this system itself processes (see Q-PAY-001); in-store card-present disputes on a POS-only sales channel are a separate, currently unmodeled boundary, not covered by this capability.

capabilities.name: Shipment Creation & Tracking
capabilities.description: A shipment record is created for an order, a tracking number and label are obtained, and delivery status (in transit, delivered, exception) is tracked through to completion or cancellation. Requires CAP-PRODUCTS because rate/label generation needs the product's own weight and dimensions, not just the order line items. Per-carrier account credentials, service codes, and API/webhook integration are explicitly out of scope and sit behind DER-CARRIER-ADAPTER; this capability owns the shipment/tracking domain data, not any single carrier's protocol. Other capabilities whose own description or obligations mention a "shipment" (e.g. CAP-RETURNS' return-shipment step, CAP-ORDER-SPLIT's per-warehouse shipments, CAP-CLICK-COLLECT's ship-to-customer path) refer to this same shipment record when this capability is also selected, not a parallel shipment concept of their own.

capabilities.name: Shipping Rate Quoting
capabilities.description: Available carrier rates for a shipment are calculated and compared by weight, dimensions, and destination, so staff or an automated policy can select a shipping method by cost or speed. This only answers what a carrier would charge to move a given package; it does not decide what the customer is charged for shipping, is discounted, or is offered as free above a threshold -- that pricing decision belongs to the checkout/pricing layer (see CAP-PROMO-RULES' buy-X-get-Y/threshold scope).

capabilities.name: Pickup Point / Convenience Store Delivery
capabilities.description: A customer can choose a convenience store or another predefined pickup location as the delivery destination instead of a self-entered address, while shipment creation and tracking still go through the same shipment record.

capabilities.name: Outsourced Fulfillment (3PL)
capabilities.description: A third-party logistics provider picks, packs, and ships orders out of its own warehouse on the merchant's behalf, holding the merchant's own stock. Requires CAP-INVENTORY because the merchant still owns and tracks this stock, unlike CAP-DROPSHIP, where the supplier ships its own goods and the merchant never holds the inventory at all.

capabilities.name: Carrier Provider Boundary
capabilities.description: Carrier/logistics provider integration sits behind an owned adapter boundary, not a direct dependency on any single carrier's API, label format, or tracking webhook shape.

capabilities.name: Own-Brand Product Development
capabilities.description: Tracks a self-designed or OEM/ODM product through its own development lifecycle -- idea, sample, sample approval, and specification version -- up to the point it is approved for production and ready to be listed for sale, distinct from CAP-PRODUCTS, which only holds the resulting sellable listing once development is done. A sample or specification version advances through a defined sign-off step before moving to the next stage, the same intrinsic sign-off-within-a-workflow pattern CAP-PROCUREMENT and CAP-RETURNS already use without depending on the separate, opt-in CAP-APPROVAL engine (which represents a configurable cross-cutting approval-workflow feature, not any process that happens to have a decision point). Requires CAP-VENDOR-MGMT because a self-developed product is made through a supplier/manufacturer relationship this capability references but does not itself own. Does not own actual production scheduling or shop-floor manufacturing execution (a full manufacturing execution system, MES); it stops at 'approved for production'.

capabilities.name: Bill of Materials
capabilities.description: The materials, components, and quantities that make up a self-developed product are recorded as a bill of materials, used to calculate the product's internal material cost and to track what changed between specification versions. This is an internal costing reference only -- it never decides what a customer is charged at checkout; that pricing decision belongs to CAP-CHANNEL-PRICING/CAP-PROMOTIONS. Also distinct from CAP-INVENTORY-COSTING, which computes inventory value and cost-of-goods-sold from actual stock movements (FIFO/weighted-average) for financial statements; a BOM's material-cost estimate is a design-time reference that may inform, but is not itself, that inventory valuation. Requires CAP-PRODUCT-DEVELOPMENT because a bill of materials only exists for a product this business is itself developing, not a product bought ready-made for resale.

capabilities.name: Quality Inspection & Defect Tracking
capabilities.description: Incoming or outgoing product inspections record findings against a defined checklist, and a defect found during inspection creates a quality issue that can be assigned a corrective action (CAPA) and tracked through to resolution. Applies to any product in the catalog, whether self-developed or bought ready-made for resale -- inspecting goods received from a supplier does not require having designed the product -- so this deliberately does not require CAP-PRODUCT-DEVELOPMENT. "Supplier" here is narrative context (which party shipped the goods being inspected), not an owned entity this capability manages; it deliberately does not require CAP-VENDOR-MGMT (unlike CAP-PRODUCT-DEVELOPMENT, which does, because it actually tracks a supplier relationship for sourcing/development) -- an inspection record references a shipment/receipt, not a vendor profile. When CAP-RETURNS is also selected, the receiving-inspection step of a customer return composes with this capability's own inspection/quality-issue records instead of a second, parallel inspection concept; when CAP-RETURNS is not selected, a returned item's inspection is out of this capability's scope. When CAP-REVIEWS is also selected, a defect reported through a product review can be aggregated into the same quality-issue record rather than tracked as a separate, parallel complaint.

capabilities.name: Product Recall
capabilities.description: A safety or quality defect confirmed through CAP-QUALITY-INSPECTION triggers a recall: the affected product (at the product/SKU level) is matched against which orders -- and therefore which customers -- actually received it, so those customers can be proactively notified and the affected units collected or replaced, distinct from CAP-RETURNS, where the customer initiates contact simply because they no longer want an undamaged product. Requires CAP-ORDERS and CAP-CUSTOMER-DATA because a recall is unexecutable without knowing which orders and customers received the affected product, the same reasoning CAP-CHARGEBACK and CAP-RISK-SCREENING already use for needing to identify a customer. Batch/lot-level traceability (narrowing a recall to only the specific production lot rather than every order of that product/SKU) is explicitly out of scope for this capability -- neither CAP-INVENTORY nor CAP-ORDERS carries lot-level granularity anywhere in this catalog, and adding it would be a real, separate capability, not an implicit part of this one. Does not decide legal/regulatory recall authority or reporting obligations itself -- compliance authority is out of this module's scope -- it only tracks the operational workflow of identifying and reaching affected customers.

capabilities.name: Merchant-Controlled Ranking & Curation
capabilities.description: A merchandising rule (boost, bury, pin-to-top, or a curated named featured set) overrides the default product ranking or inclusion on any listing surface -- search results, category/collection browsing, or a featured placement -- distinct from CAP-SEARCH, which only provides full-text retrieval, and CAP-FILTERS, which only lets the customer narrow results by their own chosen criteria. This capability deliberately requires neither: a merchant with only category/filter browsing and no search box, only a search box and no dedicated filter UI, both, or neither, can still curate what ranks where, because a merchandising rule overrides the default listing order regardless of which surface produces that listing. Also distinct from CAP-AI-RECOMMEND, an algorithmically-generated ranking signal, not a merchant-authored override -- the two can coexist without either requiring the other. Requires CAP-INVENTORY because demoting or accurately marking an out-of-stock product is an explicit acceptance criterion of this capability, not an incidental detail, and that needs real, current stock data, never an assumed or stale flag. This only reorders or curates which already-priced products are shown and in what order; it never changes a product's price or what a customer pays -- that decision remains CAP-CHANNEL-PRICING/CAP-PROMOTIONS' scope, which is why this capability carries no Q-COM-001 ('charges customers') gate.

capabilities.name: Shopping / Ad Channel Product Feeds
capabilities.description: Product price, availability, and each channel's own required attributes are packaged into a feed for an external shopping or advertising channel (e.g. Google Merchant Center, Meta Catalog, Pinterest, TikTok), and feed-quality triage flags rejected products, missing required attributes, and price or availability mismatches the channel reports back, traced to the specific source field responsible rather than reported as an opaque failure. Distinct from CAP-MULTI-MARKETPLACE/CAP-MARKETPLACE-SYNC, where the sale itself completes on a third-party marketplace and price/inventory are kept in sync bidirectionally with it; here the channel only displays the listing or serves an ad, the transaction still completes on the merchant's own storefront, and the feed is a one-way publish the channel never writes back to as authoritative. Also distinct from CAP-CAMPAIGNS, which only tracks an ad campaign's own budget, schedule, and performance, never product-level feed data. Requires CAP-INVENTORY for the same reason CAP-MARKETPLACE-SYNC already requires it: a channel feed publishes current stock availability alongside price, never a stale or assumed value. This only publishes a product's existing, already-resolved price to the channel and flags a channel-reported price mismatch for correction; it never sets or adjusts what a customer pays -- that decision remains CAP-CHANNEL-PRICING/CAP-PROMOTIONS' scope, which is why this capability carries no Q-COM-001 ('charges customers') gate.

capabilities.name: Multi-Location Stock Tracking
capabilities.description: Stock is held at two or more distinct physical locations (own warehouses, retail stores, or an outsourced 3PL warehouse), and each location carries its own independently tracked available quantity, so availability can be answered per location, stock can be moved between locations through a recorded transfer, and fulfillment can be sourced from a specific location rather than only a single company-wide total. Requires CAP-INVENTORY because a location-level balance is a partition of that capability's own stock record, never a second, parallel stock record. Distinct from CAP-POS-INVENTORY-SYNC/CAP-MARKETPLACE-SYNC, which keep one canonical stock figure consistent across sales channels; this capability partitions that same canonical record across physical locations instead -- the two compose, because a channel can be given the company-wide aggregate across all locations or a declared location subset, and either way there remains exactly one canonical stock record underneath. Deliberately does not require CAP-ORDERS: a merchant can hold stock at, and transfer stock between, multiple warehouses or stores with no order/transaction of any kind ever recorded (e.g. redistributing initial stock across new store locations before the business has taken its first sale), so adding that edge would force a merchant who explicitly answered no to having any orders/transactions into a plan that also enables order-taking. When CAP-ORDERS is also selected, an allocation always names its source location and can never exceed that location's own available quantity -- a per-location no-oversell check, distinct from and stronger than a company-wide aggregate check alone. An inbound receipt (new stock arriving at a location, e.g. from a supplier) is recorded the same way as an inter-location transfer -- a movement into a location's balance -- except it names no source location, only a destination; it is not a separate mechanism. Warehouse-internal execution -- bin/shelf addressing, putaway, pick/pack waves, barcode scanning, lot/serial/expiry tracking -- is explicitly out of scope; this capability only partitions and moves quantities between named locations, not what happens physically inside one.

capabilities.name: Inventory Cycle Count
capabilities.description: A physical stock count at a location is periodically compared against the system's recorded balance for that same stock, and any discrepancy found is recorded as an explicit, attributable adjustment movement -- who counted, when, and the before/after quantity -- never a silent overwrite of the balance, reinforcing the same immutable-movement-ledger invariant CAP-INVENTORY's own domain obligations already require for every other balance change. Requires only CAP-INVENTORY, not CAP-MULTI-LOCATION-STOCK: a single-location merchant can cycle count their one stock record exactly the same way a multi-location merchant counts each location's balance separately; multiple locations are not a precondition for this capability to be meaningful.

capabilities.name: 全通路訊息平台整合
capabilities.description: 客戶可以透過 LINE 官方帳號、WhatsApp Business、Telegram、Instagram/Messenger 等外部通訊平台傳訊息給客服，不同平台的對話統一進到同一個收件匣供客服回覆與追蹤，跟只能在自家網站或 App 裡即時打字對話的 CAP-LIVE-CHAT 不同，也不是 CAP-TICKETING 把問題建成工單追蹤的方式。

capabilities.name: Agentic Commerce Delegated Checkout
capabilities.description: A third-party AI shopping agent, acting on a customer's behalf under a verifiable, scoped purchase mandate the customer explicitly grants (spending limit, product scope, expiry), can create a checkout intent and place an order without a human directly operating the storefront UI; the mandate is verified and its scope checked before any order is created. Distinct from CAP-AI-EXTERNAL/CAP-MULTI-AGENT, which model this system's own AI calling out or coordinating internally -- here an external agent acts inward, the opposite direction.

capabilities.name: Data Retention Policy
capabilities.description: Each category of stored personal data has an explicit, enforced retention period after which it is automatically archived or deleted, rather than being kept indefinitely by default.

capabilities.name: Right to Erasure
capabilities.description: A customer or data-subject-access request can trigger deletion of that person's personal data across the system's records, not just a single table, fulfilling GDPR/CCPA erasure obligations rather than only supporting export (see CAP-CUSTOMER-EXPORT, which lets a customer take a copy of their data but does not delete it).

capabilities.name: 行銷活動歸因分析
capabilities.description: 追蹤客戶在成交前接觸過哪些行銷活動與管道，依規則把最終成交分配歸因到這些接觸點，判斷哪個活動真正帶來業績，而不是只看最後一次點擊。跟 CAP-AFFILIATE-ATTRIBUTION 不同：那是專門追蹤聯盟連結／推薦碼成交的歸因，這裡是涵蓋所有行銷活動與管道的一般性歸因分析。

capabilities.name: Feature Flags / Progressive Rollout
capabilities.description: Engineering features can be toggled on/off or rolled out to a percentage of users via runtime configuration rather than a code deploy, with per-user/segment targeting and a control-group holdout for measuring impact. Distinct from CAP-AB-TESTING, which is scoped specifically to marketing-content tests (landing pages/emails), not general engineering rollout, targeting, or statistical holdouts.

capabilities.name: Product Attribute & Taxonomy Governance
capabilities.description: Products carry a structured, governed set of attributes (e.g. color, size, material) and are mapped into a category/taxonomy tree, with attribute definitions and category mappings managed centrally rather than as free-text fields per product. Distinct from CAP-PRODUCTS, which only asserts that a product catalog exists as a domain entity, with no claim about attribute or taxonomy governance.

capabilities.name: Data Completeness & Quality Scoring
capabilities.description: Records (starting with the product catalog) are automatically checked against completeness and quality rules -- required fields present, values well-formed, no contradictory data -- and given a completeness/quality score, surfacing what's missing or wrong proactively rather than only discovering it when a downstream channel or process fails. Distinct from CAP-PRODUCT-FEED's feed-quality triage, which only flags issues a specific external shopping/ad channel reports back after publish.

capabilities.name: Inbound Webhook Idempotency
capabilities.description: Every inbound webhook from an external connector (messaging platform, third-party API, or bulk import/export integration) is verified and processed idempotently -- a redelivered or duplicate webhook event never produces a duplicate side effect.

capabilities.name: 供應商最低訂購量與交貨前置時間
capabilities.description: 記錄每個供應商對特定品項要求的最低訂購量（下單至少要訂多少），以及供應商報價的交貨前置時間（下單後大約多久會到貨），下採購單時可以據此判斷數量門檻與預估到貨時間。跟 CAP-MOQ 方向相反：CAP-MOQ 是本公司要求買方客戶至少要訂多少（b2b 模組），這裡是供應商要求本公司至少要訂多少，兩者不可互相取代。

capabilities.name: 罐頭訊息／快速回覆範本
capabilities.description: 客服人員可在工單或對話中直接套用預先寫好的罐頭訊息／快速回覆範本，不需每次重新輸入常見問題的答案；跟 CAP-AI-GENERATE 每次即時生成內容不同，這裡是人工維護的固定文字範本庫。

capabilities.name: 文件範本自動產生
capabilities.description: 可以用預先定義好的文件範本，帶入變數自動產生標準化文件（例如常見問題頁面、政策公告、說明手冊），不需每次手動重新排版撰寫；跟 CAP-KNOWLEDGE-BASE 收錄固定知識文章不同，這裡是動態帶入變數產生文件的能力，且依附於知識庫已存在為前提。

capabilities.name: AI 字幕／隱藏式字幕生成
capabilities.description: 影片可以自動產生多語言字幕／隱藏式字幕並對齊時間軸，不需人工逐句聽打與翻譯；跟一般性 AI 生成（CAP-AI-GENERATE）或介面語系支援（CAP-I18N）不同，這裡專門處理影片時間軸對齊字幕，且依附於影片內容已產出為前提。

capabilities.name: Marketplace Taxonomy/Attribute Mapping
capabilities.description: Maps the merchant's own governed product category/attribute structure (CAP-PRODUCT-ATTRIBUTES) to each connected marketplace's own, differently-shaped taxonomy and required-attribute schema, so a listing satisfies that marketplace's specific category/attribute rules. Distinct from CAP-MULTI-MARKETPLACE, which only syncs the listing/offer itself, not the category/attribute translation between two different taxonomies.

capabilities.name: Marketplace Listing Error Handling
capabilities.description: Collects and categorizes a connected marketplace's listing rejection, review-failure, or policy-violation responses so the merchant knows exactly which field or rule caused the rejection and can fix and resubmit it. Distinct from CAP-PRODUCT-FEED's feed-quality triage, which is scoped to non-transactional shopping/ad feed channels (Google Merchant Center, Meta Catalog), not transactional marketplace listings (Amazon, Shopee, etc.).

capabilities.name: Marketplace Buyer Messaging
capabilities.description: Buyer-seller messages sent through a connected marketplace's own native messaging system (e.g. Amazon Seller Messaging, Shopee Chat) are received and replied to within that marketplace's own policy and response-time rules. Distinct from CAP-LIVE-CHAT (in-site chat) and CAP-TICKETING (internal ticket workflow), neither of which represents a marketplace's own buyer-messaging channel.

capabilities.name: Order Merge
capabilities.description: Multiple separate orders (e.g. placed separately by the same customer, or destined for the same fulfillment location) can be combined into a single fulfillment/shipment unit before pick-pack -- the inverse operation of CAP-ORDER-SPLIT -- and the merged shipment always traces back to every original order it was merged from.

capabilities.name: Fulfillment Routing Rules
capabilities.description: An order line is automatically routed to whichever warehouse, store, or 3PL fulfillment source a configured rule set determines (e.g. nearest location, lowest stock-holding cost, availability), and can be manually rerouted afterward if the originally assigned source becomes unavailable; distinct from CAP-ORDER-SPLIT, which only divides an order's lines across multiple shipments without deciding which source fulfills each one.

capabilities.name: Order Exception Management
capabilities.description: An order-fulfillment problem (failed allocation, fulfillment-source rejection, address/inventory mismatch) is raised as an explicit, trackable exception record requiring resolution, rather than the order silently stalling in an undefined state or only surfacing as an unattributed FOUND-ERROR log entry.

capabilities.name: POS Receipt Generation
capabilities.description: A point-of-sale transaction produces a printed or emailed receipt itemizing the purchased line items, tax, and payment method at the moment of sale; distinct from CAP-INVOICES, which is scoped to formal billable business transactions, not point-of-sale receipts.

capabilities.name: AI Prompt Registry
capabilities.description: Prompts used to drive AI features are stored, versioned, and reused from a central registry rather than hardcoded inline per call site, so a prompt change is tracked and attributable to a specific prompt version rather than an untraceable inline edit.

capabilities.name: AI Output Evaluation
capabilities.description: AI-generated outputs are automatically scored against defined quality/correctness criteria (golden test sets, rubric-based grading) before or after being surfaced, so a quality regression from a model, prompt, or provider change is caught rather than only discovered by end users.

capabilities.name: AI Answer Source Citation
capabilities.description: An AI-generated answer surfaces the specific source document(s)/passage(s) it was derived from as a user-facing citation, so the answer's provenance is traceable and verifiable by the end user -- distinct from FOUND-EVIDENCE, which only requires that evidence exist and be reproducible internally for governance purposes, not that it be surfaced to the end user as a citation.

capabilities.name: Workflow Step Retry
capabilities.description: A failed automation workflow step -- any step, not only the payment- and AI-specific idempotent retries DER-PAYMENT-IDEMPOTENCY/DER-AI-IDEMPOTENCY already cover -- can be automatically retried with a defined backoff/limit, or resumed manually from the point of failure, without re-executing already-completed steps or duplicating their side effects.

capabilities.name: Business Policy Engine
capabilities.description: Business rules (eligibility conditions, thresholds, approval-routing logic) are authored and evaluated as declarative policy definitions consumed by workflow steps, rather than hardcoded per workflow, so a policy change does not require a code change to the workflow that consumes its result.

capabilities.name: Task Checklist / Sub-tasks
capabilities.description: A task can have an ordered list of checklist sub-items that are each independently checked off, with the parent task's completion optionally requiring every sub-item to be checked; distinct from CAP-TASKS' own single task-level assignment and status.

capabilities.name: Experiment Results & Statistical Metrics
capabilities.description: A running experiment's variant groups (as defined by CAP-FEATURE-FLAGS' rollout/targeting/holdout mechanism) are measured against defined success metrics with statistical-significance calculation (sample size, confidence interval), producing a result a decision-maker can act on; distinct from CAP-FEATURE-FLAGS itself, which only controls exposure, never measures outcome.

capabilities.name: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA/MFA)
capabilities.description: A user can enable a second authentication factor (TOTP authenticator app, SMS/email one-time code) in addition to their password, and the system can require it at login; distinct from CAP-SSO, which delegates authentication to an external enterprise identity provider rather than adding a second factor to this system's own credential.

capabilities.name: Per-Connector Usage Entitlement
capabilities.description: Each connected third-party integration/connector carries its own usage quota as a distinct entitlement dimension (e.g. one plan allows 2 connected marketplaces, another allows 10), checked and enforced independently from the account's other usage-metering dimensions.

capabilities.name: Search Autocomplete / Typeahead
capabilities.description: As a user types a search query, the system suggests likely completions or matching terms in real time before the query is submitted, drawn from the same indexed catalog CAP-SEARCH queries against; distinct from CAP-SEARCH's own retrieval of an already-submitted query.

capabilities.name: Subscription Churn Analytics
capabilities.description: Subscriber cancellation/non-renewal is tracked and analyzed to compute a churn rate and surface at-risk subscribers (e.g. by usage decline or repeated failed payment attempts) before they cancel, rather than only recording the cancellation event after the fact.

capabilities.name: Creator Product Seeding
capabilities.description: Product units can be gifted or shipped to a creator or influencer at no cost, as part of a seeding campaign, tracked against that creator's own record distinct from a paid affiliate commission transaction.

capabilities.name: UGC Usage Rights Licensing
capabilities.description: A creator's submitted content (photo, video, post) can have an explicit usage-rights grant recorded -- scope, duration, and channels the merchant is permitted to reuse it on -- before the merchant reuses that content in its own marketing, rather than assuming implicit permission from the partnership relationship alone. Distinct from CAP-UGC, which only stores/serves user-generated content generically and does not track reuse permission.

capabilities.name: Overstock Detection
capabilities.description: Stock significantly exceeding projected demand for its holding-cost/shelf-life horizon is automatically flagged as overstock, using the same forecast CAP-DEMAND-FORECAST already produces, so a merchant can act (mark down for clearance, reallocate stock, or halt further reordering) before capital is tied up in excess inventory.

capabilities.name: Inventory Aging
capabilities.description: Each stock unit/batch's time-in-stock since receipt is tracked and surfaced by age band (e.g. 0-30/31-60/60+ days), distinct from CAP-AR-AGING, which ages receivables, not physical stock.

capabilities.name: Semantic Metric Governance
capabilities.description: A business metric (e.g. "active customer", "units shipped per week") is defined once as a named, versioned calculation registered centrally, and every report, dashboard, or data-warehouse consumer resolves that metric from the same registered definition, rather than each consumer recomputing its own ad hoc version that can silently disagree with another.
